coveragePolicy.boundaryConvention: Both UTC midnight endpoints included in sample arrays; interval durations exclude the final endpoint.
coveragePolicy.leapDayPolicy: February 29 anniversaries clamp to February 28 in non-leap years.
coveragePolicy.refreshPolicy: Regenerate for the current UTC date once daily; advancing the date drops the oldest coverage and adds the new end. Deployment scheduling is external to this generator.

conventions.elevation: deg above the local horizontal plane (sphere normal, R = 1737.4 km)
conventions.frame: MOON_ME (NAIF moon_de440_250416.tf: DE440 PA rotated to DE421 mean-Earth, same frame as LOLA/PGDA DEMs)
conventions.time: UTC; sample i at startUtc + i*stepMinutes; both endpoint samples stored. Metrics use the N-1 left-endpoint 5-minute intervals, excluding the terminal sample from durations/averages.
conventions.solarEclipse: Opaque spherical Earth and uniform solar disk in an angular tangent plane; integrate the disk jointly above the local horizontal terrain cut and outside Earth. No atmosphere, refraction, limb darkening, irradiance or energy model.
conventions.heightCalculation: Shared azDeg, elDeg, angularRadiusDeg and rangeKm refer to the 1 m observer. Each height has separately computed observer position, horizon, visible fractions, events and metrics; no interpolation between heights.
conventions.visibleFraction: fraction of the body's disk above the terrain horizon; solar fractions additionally exclude Earth-occulted area. Horizontal terrain cut at disk-centre azimuth; uniform disks. Solar terrain-only and eclipse-only fractions are separately published and are not multiplied.
conventions.censored: true when the longest period touches the start or end of the simulated window: show as >= value

aiDisclosure: The pipeline code in scientific/ was written with AI coding assistants (Claude Opus 5.5; reviewed with Codex). Every number in public/data/ is computed deterministically by that code from NASA PDS/PGDA LOLA data and NAIF SPICE kernels; no value was produced or edited by a language model.
assumptions: Bare-terrain horizon from LOLA DEMs: 5 m PGDA (<5 km), 80 m PDS (5-100 km), 240 m PDS (>100 km), 720 azimuths, great-circle sight lines, exact spherical geometry.
Observer heights 0.5, 1, 2, 5 and 10 m above the local terrain surface; heights describe the model observer, not DEM vertical accuracy.
Sun and Earth treated as uniform disks; Earth visibility is geometric line of sight only.

Solar eclipses use an opaque spherical Earth (6378.137 km) and angular-circle approximation; fractional solar area jointly excludes terrain and Earth. No atmospheric transmission, refraction, limb darkening, penumbral photometry or energy calculation.

eclipseUnobscuredFraction is the Sun area not covered by Earth before terrain; terrainVisibleFraction ignores Earth; visibleFraction applies the union of both occluders. Eclipse contact events are separate from terrain events.
Durations and metrics from a 5-min grid; rise/set times refined by bisection to <= 30 s and reported with 1-min resolution.
limitations: Four original points from published LOLA studies and two neighboring points selected by our team using fixed map-coordinate offsets; none are NASA-selected landing sites or mission recommendations.
No power, battery, thermal, communications-link (DSN), landing-safety or hazard assessment.
Visibility windows shorter than the internal grid step may be missed.

DEM interpolation, boulders and sub-pixel relief are not modelled; near-field horizon is sensitive to DEM error at low observer heights, especially 0.5 m and 1 m (Barker et al. 2021); a 0.5 m model height does not imply 0.5 m terrain accuracy.
Results only cover the stated period; dates outside it are not computed.
